title: Dealing with Increased Incidence of Tuberculosis Cases
what_it_is: Dealing with Increased Incidence of Tuberculosis Cases

sections.label: TB incidence and latent TB
sections.summary: Active TB incidence rates were similar in 2017 and 2018, and up to 30% have latent TB, which is not infectious.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: The incidence rates of active tuberculosis (TB) cases in 2017 and 2018 were similar, at 39 cases per 100,000 resident population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: In 2018, almost half of new active TB cases were aged 60 and older, although their incidence rates had also remained stable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: As such, up to 30% have latent TB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: Latent TB patients do not exhibit symptoms and are not infectious, but one in 10 may progress to active TB during their lifetime.

sections.label: TBCU contact investigations
sections.summary: The Tuberculosis Control Unit conducts contact investigations to identify persons with close and prolonged contact with infectious TB cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: To contain TB transmission, the Tuberculosis Control Unit (TBCU) conducts contact investigations to identify persons who have had close and prolonged contact with infectious TB cases.

sections.label: MDR-TB isolation and treatment
sections.summary: MDR-TB patients are isolated about two months and undergo directly observed therapy for about two years, with rapid DNA tests adopted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: For Multi-Drug Resistant TB (MDR-TB), patients are isolated for treatment until they become non-infectious, which takes about two months, and they will undergo directly observed therapy (DOT) for about two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: We have also adopted new technologies, such as rapid DNA tests for drug resistance, reducing time taken for identification of MDR-TB from two months to a few hours to facilitate early intervention.

sections.label: Long-term TB control goal
sections.summary: Setting a firm TB control target is difficult, but the longer-term goal is to benchmark against high-income countries with rates under 20 per 100,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: Hence, it is quite difficult to set a firm target to achieve firm TB control.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: But in the longer term, our goal is to benchmark ourselves against high-income countries that have TB rates of about less than 20 cases per 100,000 population.
